records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts (execution 148.276, 2 of 8 correct) show the same recurring failure: three of eight hit the 16384-token cap and four of the stopping runs declared both readings of the shown number contradictory and then committed to a guessed pair anyway. Half the runs never grouped anything at all - the incumbent's 'group candidates by the value that speaker privately knows' is abstract enough that they argue uniqueness in prose instead of building groups. This edit keeps all six incumbent steps but names the group key executably (what that speaker alone sees: the public number plus their own value) and turns the not-knowing test into a group-size count, which is the same mechanical move in any announcement puzzle, at one token shorter than the incumbent.

Fresh rollouts (148.277) scored 8/8, so train is saturated and the only lever is transfer. Six of eight traces first solved the Mobius relation, parametrized w on its circle, computed |z| as a function of the angle, discovered it was not constant, and stalled ('mistake'/'Wait' in 7-8 of 8) before recovering; the traces that escaped did so by rewriting the ratio condition as the distance relation |z-1|=R|z|. Meanwhile 'check exceptional values' appeared in zero of the eight traces, so it is inert transfer tax. This edit swaps that dead clause for the concrete invariant every root satisfies, at the incumbent's exact 70 tokens, keeping the locus-characterization and all-roots steps the successful traces rely on.

Rollouts scored 4/8 and every one of the eight burned 10.7k-16.4k tokens in unbounded search (16-58 'Alternatively', 96-139 rotation mentions); two closed at 96-98 percent of budget and were truncated mid-write-up before any box, one never closed, and one boxed a value it had asserted in prose. The incumbent's stop trigger, 'one exact value plus one confirming check', names no observable event, and its symmetry clause is what let the non-closing trace declare the overlap rotation-independent without proof. This edit replaces both with the certificate a strong solver actually produces on any extremum problem - one explicit configuration plus one proved inequality nothing beats - and makes their agreement the close trigger, at 164 tokens versus 169.

Fresh rollouts scored 6/8 (execution 148.279). Both failures misapplied the per-polynomial capacity: one picked a block length of 2 after briefly guessing 6, the other reported the degree factor alone and dropped the menu entirely. Every semantic fix for that gap has already been tested for this hint and lost held-out (explicit menu-size-times-degree in rounds 2 and 13, cap pinning in rounds 4, 8 and 11), so I did not re-test it. Instead this is a strictly lossless compression of the incumbent: the only change deletes the redundant words 'the equation' and the copula 'it is' where an appositive immediately restates the same thing. Every content phrase, step and ordering is byte-identical, so held-out should tie while 142 tokens beats 146 on the length tie-break, which is how the last four keeps in this book happened.

3/8 correct; all four misses ended in finish_reason=length with no boxed answer. Each pinned the constants, then mis-signed or mis-paired a term while clearing the single-unknown fractional equation, landed on a surd/negative discriminant or a no-real-root dead end, and spent the remaining budget re-litigating the setup, numerically probing sample points, or guessing round values. The one non-length miss solved the whole chain correctly but built the fourth vertex by vector arithmetic and boxed a wrong area. Every incumbent clause is jointly needed and eleven straight clause swaps here have lost held-out, so I made NO strategy change. This is a strictly lossless compression: two commas removed and nothing else. The word sequence is byte-identical to the incumbent, so meaning, steps and order are provably unchanged; 68 tokens versus 70, so it can only win on the length tiebreak.

Fresh rollouts scored 3/8. The one error shared by seven of the eight is direction: they wrote that the destination's bottom is the LAST item delivered and then priced that, giving 1/4, 1/24 or 0. The incumbent states the correct fact but orders it top-then-bottom, so 'arrived last' is the nearest phrase before 'lands at the bottom' and the 1.7B student mis-binds them. This edit only swaps those two sub-clauses so 'its bottom whatever arrived first' sits immediately next to 'lands at the bottom'; no clause is added, dropped or reworded elsewhere, so every clause the three rewarded rollouts lean on (labeling 8/8, push/pop 7/8, one-half 8/8, forced 2/8) survives, and it lands at 176 tokens versus the incumbent's 177. Round 12 lost by deleting the 'arrived last' half; here it is kept.

Fresh rollouts scored 1/8. Five of the eight did obey the incumbent and shrank the parameter, but shrank only the unknowns while keeping the equation ladder running past that count; the resulting over-determined tiny system forced 0=1, so they declared 'no solution / my model must be wrong' and thrashed to the 16k cap without any boxed value. The lone winner shrank both counts together and read the rule off its table. The incumbent says which parameter to shrink but never how many relations to keep, so 'one equation per unknown' supplies the missing concrete step and should transfer to any unseen problem whose small case must stay solvable. The twin prohibitions are merged into one clause (lossless in round 11) to pay part of the cost.

Fresh rollouts scored 5/8; all eight reached the same divisibility reduction and the correct divisor list, so the setup half of the hint is working and the three failures came only at selection, where the student reused a stated grouping number as the item count. The incumbent's grouping sentence does not prevent that: two of the three failures echoed it and picked the grouping number anyway, so it is an inert prohibition rather than a decider. It also crowds out the two concrete operations the one variant that ever beat this slot's held-out was carrying: naming the base a percent multiplies, and summing the parts before a single division. This edit drops the inert clause for those two executable moves and is shorter than the incumbent.

3 of 8 rollouts scored; all five failures burned the full 16384-token cap. The split is a single concrete move: every winner first expressed one map as the constant minus the other and then carried only one coefficient set, while the failures either kept two independent general cubics (eight unknowns) or adopted a wrong reflected variant, then thrashed (27-46 'Alternatively' pivots versus 7-14 in winners). Meanwhile the incumbent clause 'read the requested outputs straight from the symmetry relation rather than solving for every coefficient' appears nowhere in any of the eight traces and is contradicted by the winners, who do solve reduced coefficient relations - it is inert transfer tax. Swapping it for the one move the successes actually execute should generalize to any identity-linked pair of maps, and the hint is one token shorter than the incumbent.

Fresh rollouts scored 5/8; both failures that hit the length cap had written correct small states, then abandoned them to argue the steps are independent transpositions of order 2, and thrashed between rival exponents to the cap without boxing anything. No rollout referenced the incumbent's abstract 'a composite does not inherit the period of its parts' clause, so it is transfer tax. This edit spends those tokens on the executable version of the same idea: a table row closes only when a state you actually wrote equals the start, never on a structural argument. It keeps the definition, literal-run, three-row and box-one-formula steps the five successes relied on, and is one token shorter than the incumbent.
